paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to the "Company," "we," "us" or "our" refer to Utz Brands, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Our core geographies consist of Alabama, Connecticut, Delaware, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, and West Virginia, with the rest of the U.S. representing our expansion geographies.

We were founded in 1921 in Hanover, Pennsylvania and benefit from over 100 years of brand awareness and heritage in the salty snack industry. We are a leading United States manufacturer of branded salty snacks, producing a broad offering of salty snacks, including potato chips, tortilla chips, pretzels, cheese snacks, pork skins, pub/party mixes and other snacks. Our iconic portfolio of authentic, craft and "better-for-you" ("BFY") brands includes Utz®, On The Border®, Zapp's®, Boulder Canyon®, Golden Flake®, Hawaiian® Brand and Miguelito's®, among others, and enjoys strong household penetration in the United States, where our products can be found in approximately 50% of U.S. households as of December 28, 2025. As of December 28, 2025, we operate eight primary manufacturing facilities across the United States with a broad range of capabilities. Our products are distributed nationally to grocery, mass merchant, club, convenience, drug and other retailers through direct shipments, distributors and approximately 2,500 direct-store delivery ("DSD") routes. We have historically expanded our geographic reach and product portfolio organically and through acquisitions. Based on 2025 retail sales, we are the second-largest producer of branded salty snacks in our collective core geographies of Alabama, Connecticut, Delaware, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, and West Virginia (our "Core Geographies," and all other states in the United States, our "Expansion Geographies"), where we have acquired strong regional brands and distribution capabilities in recent years.

Our business benefits from multiple opportunities to deliver attractive long-term profitable growth. Our value creation strategies are focused on driving productivity to enhance margins, reinvesting in marketing and innovation to accelerate revenue growth and continuing to make strategic acquisitions. We believe we are well-positioned for long-term growth in the salty snack industry as we (a) gained a significant amount of new customers over the past several years, (b) have significant opportunity in our Expansion Geographies and under-penetrated channels, (c) continue to execute productivity efforts that we believe will help to fuel incremental marketing and innovation to accelerate growth in sales relative to our peers, (d) continue to make infrastructure improvements to enable us to continue to scale to greater heights, and (e) continue to make strategic acquisitions that deliver strong synergies and that enhance our competitive positioning. We believe each of these growth avenues represents a sizeable opportunity to expand our net sales. In addition, we further anticipate expanding our margins over the long term through supply chain productivity, revenue management, a higher-margin product mix, and higher margins on incremental sales as we leverage our scalable existing platform.

The Company has focused on increasing manufacturing and streamlining distribution. During fiscal years 2023 and 2024, the Company bought out and terminated the contracts of multiple distributors who had previously been providing services to the Company. These transactions were accounted for as asset purchases and contract terminations, respectively, and resulted in expense of $1.5 million and $2.1 million for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2023 and December 29, 2024, respectively.

On February 5, 2024, the Company sold certain assets and brands to affiliates of Our Home™, an operating company of Better-for-You brands ("Our Home"). Under the agreement, affiliates of Our Home purchased the Good Health and R.W. Garcia brands, and the Lincolnton, NC and Lititz, PA manufacturing facilities and certain related assets, and assumed the Company's Las Vegas, NV facility lease and manufacturing operations (the "Good Health and R.W. Garcia Sale"), for $167.5 million, subject to customary adjustments. See Note 2. Divestitures to our Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. On April 22, 2024, the Company also sold to Our Home its Berlin, PA and Fitchburg, MA manufacturing facilities and certain related assets, including certain inventory (the "Manufacturing Facilities Sale").

The Company and Our Home were operating under transition services agreements related to each of the Good Health and R.W. Garcia Sale and the Manufacturing Facilities Sale, which expired during the first half of 2025. For the greater part of fiscal year 2025, the parties operated under reciprocal co-manufacturing agreements. Although Our Home remains involved in the manufacturing of certain products of the Company, the Company no longer manufactures products for Good Health. Certain Good Health products continue to be distributed and sold on the Company's DSD network for Our Home, pursuant to a distribution agreement. The Company received approximately $18.7 million in advance from Our Home for certain services under these agreements, which the Company recognized through income from operations over the terms of the transition services and co-manufacturing agreements.

As part of its ongoing supply chain transformation, the Company announced in July 2025 the strategic decision to consolidate its manufacturing footprint with the closure of its Grand Rapids, Michigan manufacturing facility. This decision is a key component of the Company's long-term strategic roadmap, is expected to generate cost savings and should enable the Company to allocate more volume to its larger, more efficient facilities, while driving fixed cost leverage and enhanced automation capabilities across its remaining network. In addition to the expected cost savings, the Company expects the optimized footprint will support its ongoing geographic expansion.

In September 2025, the Company announced a multi-phase project aimed at upgrading facilities across its Hanover, PA campus. The project includes upgrading the Company's headquarters and transforming it into a modern employee hub as well as other upgrades. As part of this project, the Company intends to sell two buildings located in Hanover, PA. See Note 5. Property, Plant and Equipment, Net.

As part of the California expansion strategy, in October 2025, the Company acquired Insignia International's DSD distribution assets. The transaction includes DSD routes across California and the Midwest, along with select related assets. This acquisition accelerates Utz's expansion in California, a key growth geography that represents the largest U.S. market for salty snacks with $4.1 billion in retail sales based on Circana data.

We have a long-term growth strategy focusing on various initiatives. Our portfolio strategy is focused on accelerating investments in marketing and innovation to drive top-line growth and achieve share gains in the Salty Snack category. We plan to further penetrate our Expansion Geographies and untapped channels and customers by further expanding our Branded Salty Snacks, as defined below, in Expansion Geographies, as well as maintaining our share in our Core Geographies. We plan to transform our supply chain into a more cost-efficient and flexible system. As part of our long-term growth strategy, we intend to enhance our DSD system of IOs to further improve execution and generate higher returns and strengthen other organizational capabilities while driving down costs. Additionally, we intend to improve our balance sheet flexibility by accelerating cash generation and maintaining a disciplined capital allocation approach, which would reduce leverage while opportunistically pursuing strategic acquisitions and dispositions.

Our business is managed and reported in one operating segment due to the similar nature of all of the products that the Company sells, the functional alignment of the Company's organizational structure, and the reports that are regularly reviewed by the chief operating decision maker (the "CODM") for the purpose of assessing performance and allocating resources. However, we strategically manage our portfolio of brands by segregating our sole operating segment into Branded Salty Snacks and Non-Branded & Non-Salty Snacks. Branded Salty Snacks, in aggregate, enjoy a combination of higher growth and margins, greater potential for value-added innovation, and enhanced responsiveness to consumer marketing as compared to Non-Branded & Non-Salty Snacks. As a result, we focus our investment spending and brand-building activities on Branded Salty Snacks while managing Non-Branded & Non-Salty Snacks for cash flow generation to support investment in Branded Salty Snacks and fund other corporate priorities. We periodically assess the designation of brands within these segregations and reclassify brands based on their alignment with the criteria above.

Our Branded Salty Snacks are comprised of our Power Four Brands, consisting of our flagship Utz® brand, On The Border®, Zapp's®, and Boulder Canyon®, along with our other brands, including Golden Flake®, Miguelito's®, Hawaiian®, Bachman®, Tim's Cascade®, Dirty Potato Chips®, TGI Fridays®, and Vitner's® (our "Other Brands").

Our flagship Utz brand generated retail sales in excess of $870 million in 2025, representing an approximate 5.7% compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") (during 2021 through 2025) and making it one of the 10 largest salty snack brands in the United States by retail sales as of December 28, 2025 based on Circana data. Recognized for its iconic logo featuring the "Little Utz Girl" since the 1920s, the Utz brand currently uses the slogan "Family Crafted Flavor Since 1921". We sell a variety of salty snacks under the Utz brand, including potato chips, pretzels, cheese snacks, pub/party mixes, and seasonal favorites.

Our On The Border brand ("OTB") is a national brand of tortilla chips, salsa and queso. OTB is the #2 unflavored tortilla chip brand in the United States based on annual sales for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025. OTB supports our national geographic footprint, particularly in our Expansion Geographies, and enhances our presence in the Mass and Club retail channels.

headings: We operate in the highly competitive and increasingly consolidated snack food industry. If we are unable to compete effectively, it may reduce our ability to sell our products to our customers or consumers.
Demand for our products may be adversely affected by changes in consumer preferences and tastes or if we are unable to innovate or market our products effectively, which could reduce our revenues.
Consumers' loyalty to our brands may change due to factors beyond our control, which could have a material adverse effect on our business and operating results.
If our products become adulterated or are mislabeled, we might need to recall those items, and we may experience product liability claims and related losses, as well as damage to our reputation.
Changes in retail distribution arrangements can result in the loss of retail shelf space and disrupt sales of food products, causing our sales to fall.
The evolution of e-commerce retailers and sales channels may adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Disruption to our manufacturing operations, supply chain or distribution channels could impair our ability to produce or deliver finished products and negatively impact our operating results.

Our results of operations and profitability may continue to be adversely affected by inflation, including from rising labor costs, and we may not be able to effectively offset such inflation and volatility.
Our business, financial condition or results of operations may be adversely affected by shortages of raw materials, energy, water and other supplies.

Potential liabilities and costs from litigation, claims, legal or regulatory proceedings, inquiries or investigations can have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition or results of operations.
We may be unable to successfully identify and execute acquisitions or dispositions or to successfully integrate acquisitions or carve out dispositions.
The geographic concentration of our markets may adversely impact us if we are unable to effectively diversify the markets in which we participate.
We may not be able to attract and retain the highly skilled people we need to support our business.
Impairment in the carrying value of goodwill or other intangible assets could have an adverse impact on our financial results.
Disruptions, failures or security breaches of our information technology infrastructure could have a negative impact on our operations and subject us to significant losses.
Climate change or legal, regulatory or market measures to address climate change may negatively affect our business and operations or damage our reputation.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties. You should carefully consider the following risks as well as the other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We operate in a changing environment that involves numerous known and unknown risks and uncertainties that could materially adversely affect our operations. Any of the following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects. However, the selected risks described below are not the only risks facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or those we currently view to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects. In such a case, the trading price of our securities could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment in us.

The sales of most of our products are subject to significant competition due to factors including product quality and taste, brand awareness among consumers, access to shelf space at retail customers' locations, price, advertising and promotion, innovation of on-trend snacks, variety of snacks offered, nutritional content, product packaging and package design. We compete in the snack food market against numerous multinational, regional and local companies, as well as emerging companies, including in the BFY product subcategory, principally on the basis of product taste and quality, but also brand recognition and loyalty, price, marketing, advertising and the ability to satisfy specific consumer dietary needs.

Due to the competitive landscape in the snack food industry, price increases for our products that we initiate or failure to effectively advertise and promote our products may negatively impact our financial results if not properly implemented or accepted by our customers, IOs, third-party distributors or consumers. Substantial advertising and promotional expenditures may also be required to maintain or improve our brands' market position or to introduce a new product to the market, and participants in our industry may be engaging in new advertising trends or channels which we are not. Historically, we have offered a variety of sales and promotion incentives to our customers, IOs, third-party distributors and consumers, such as price discounts, consumer coupons, volume rebates, cooperative marketing programs, product placement fees and in-store displays, often in connection with seasonal social events, holidays and sporting events. The promotional environment has intensified in recent years, including but not limited to robust promotional launches, and we have been, and may in the future be, limited in our ability to increase prices or adjust product sizes sufficiently on a timely basis, or at all, in order to offset increased input costs, such as raw materials, packaging, energy, freight, labor, and overhead costs or other expenditures, such as advertising and promotion costs, which has the effect of reducing overall sales volume, revenue and operating profit. In addition, advertising and promotional expenditures may be ineffective if consumers prioritize price over other factors and purchase lower-cost alternatives, such as private label, generic or store branded products.

Our ability to compete may also be dependent on the availability of product category-appropriate snack aisles at our retail customers' locations and whether our products are placed in the appropriate snack aisle, such as the BFY snack food aisle or in the traditional snack food aisle. An increasing focus on BFY products and other specialty products in the marketplace will likely increase these competitive pressures within the category in future periods. Further, companies in the BFY product segment providing innovative or trendy snack foods often receive investments from private equity, venture capital or other investors, who may be more willing to accept lower product margins or sustained losses in order to gain market share. If such emerging companies are able to attract a loyal consumer base through more innovative or trendier snack foods or offer their snack food products at lower prices than us, our market share and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected.

If our advertising or promotional efforts do not increase brand awareness or sales of our products, our expenses may increase without a corresponding increase in revenue, and our operating profit may be reduced. Additionally, if market prices for certain inputs decline significantly, in some instances we may be required by contract to pay customers the difference or experience customer pressure to reduce the prices for our products, which could lower our revenue and operating profit.

There is continuing consolidation in the snack food industry and in retail outlets for snack foods by other market participants. Although we benefit from the execution of our own acquisition strategy within the snack food industry and with respect to snack distribution channels, ongoing consolidation in the snack food industry and retail outlets by others may prevent us from effectively competing if others in the industry that have greater resources than us or if retail customers or potential retail customers enter into long-term purchase contracts or promotional arrangements. Significant consolidation by others increases the possibility that we could lose one or more major customers, lose existing product authorizations or shelf space at customer locations, or lose market share. For example, our competitors vie for the same shelf placement and may offer incentives to retail customers that we cannot match, particularly as a result of consolidation. Even if we obtain shelf space or preferable shelf placement for any of our brands, our new and existing products may fail to achieve the sales expectations set by our retail customers, potentially causing these retailers to remove our products from the shelf or place them in less favorable locations. Additionally, an increase in the number and quality of private-label products in the product categories in which we compete has reduced available shelf space and could continue to hamper the placement for our branded products, which could adversely affect our sales. To obtain and keep shelf placement for our products, we may need to increase our marketing and advertising spending in order to create consumer awareness, protect and grow our existing market share or to promote new products, which could impact our operating results. We also consistently evaluate our product lines to determine whether it may be necessary to discontinue certain products. Discontinuing product lines may increase our profitability but could reduce our sales and hurt our brand and consumer loyalty, and a reduction in sales of certain of our products could result in a reduction in sales of other of our products.

Investments in new product innovation support three focus areas that are rooted in the consumer and tied to our portfolio and brand strategy: Expanding Positive Choices, Delivering Craveable Flavor, and Capturing Occasions. Within Expanding Positive Choices, recent focus has been on Boulder Canyon, a brand offering solutions for consumers seeking great tasting BFY snacks via BFY oils such as avocado oil and olive oil. Innovation contributed to Boulder Canyon® increases with the launching of new flavors that capitalized on the hot & spicy trend and by entrance into the cheese snack subcategory. Boulder Canyon® gained share for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025 versus the comparable prior year period with growth of 180.5% per Circana. In the natural channel, Boulder Canyon growth was 36.9% for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025, per Spins. Within Delivering Craveable Flavor, we recently addressed consumer desire for flavor exploration with innovation across brands and snacking subcategories via our seasoned pretzels and new potato chip flavor offerings in both our Utz and Zapp's brands. Within Capturing Occasions, we recently introduced a portfolio of variety/multipacks across our Power Four Brands, consisting of our flagship Utz® brand, On The Border®, Zapp's®, and Boulder Canyon®, and our Targeted Brands, consisting of Golden Flake®, Miguelito's®, Hawaiian®, Bachman®, Tim's Cascade®, Dirty Potato Chips®, and TGI Fridays®. During the third quarter of 2025, we announced our commitment to remove Food, Drug & Cosmetic colors from our portfolio of products before the end of 2027. While we do not currently anticipate a significant impact to our input costs in our efforts to meet this commitment, our net sales, market share, or results of operations could be adversely affected if we are unsuccessful in our efforts to continue to satisfy consumer preferences.

We regularly monitor worldwide supply and commodity costs so that we can cost-effectively secure ingredients, packaging and fuel required for production. A number of external factors such as weather, which may be impacted in unanticipated ways due to climate change, commodity market conditions, inflationary conditions and the effects of governmental, agricultural or other programs, including tariffs or other trade policies, may affect the cost and availability of raw materials and agricultural materials used in our products. Given that nearly all our input costs are sourced domestically and our manufacturing facilities are all in the United States, we continue to expect that recent tariff volatility will have a modest and manageable impact on our business in 2026. We address commodity costs primarily through the use of buying-forward, which locks in pricing for key materials between three and 18 months in advance. Other methods include hedging, net pricing adjustments to cover longer term cost inflation, and manufacturing and overhead cost control. Our hedging techniques, such as forward contracts, limit the impact of fluctuations in the cost of our principal raw materials; however, we may not be able to fully hedge against commodity cost changes, where there is a limited ability to hedge, and our hedging strategies may not protect us from increases in specific raw material costs. Commodity cost increases may adversely impact our net income. Although we have experienced some ingredient cost deflation, we continue to experience rising costs related to fuel and freight rates as well as rising labor costs both of which have negatively impacted profitability. Transportation costs have been on the rise and may continue to rise and adversely impact net income. The Company looks to offset rising costs through increasing manufacturing and distribution efficiencies as well as through price increases to our customers, although it is unclear whether historic customer sales levels will be maintained at these higher prices (See "Key Developments and Trends - Long-Term Demographics, Consumer Trends, and Demand" and "Key Developments and Trends - Competition"). Due to competitive market conditions, planned trade or promotional incentives, or other factors, our pricing actions may also lag supply and commodity cost changes.

While the costs of our principal raw materials fluctuate, we believe there will continue to be an adequate supply of the raw materials we use and that they will generally remain available from numerous sources. Market factors, including supply and demand may result in higher costs of sourcing those materials.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有要求，本年度報告表 10-K 全文提及的「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」或「我們」均指 Utz Brands, Inc. 及其合併子公司。我們的核心地理區域包括阿拉巴馬州、康乃狄克州、特拉華州、路易斯安那州、緬因州、馬裏蘭州、麻薩諸塞州、密西西比州、新罕布夏州、新澤西州、紐約州、北卡羅來納州、俄亥俄州、賓夕法尼亞州、羅德島州、南卡羅來納州、佛蒙特州、維吉尼亞州、華盛頓州及西維吉尼亞州，其餘美國地區則為我們的擴張地理區域。

我們於 1921 年在賓夕法尼亞州漢諾威成立，並受益於超過 100 年的品牌認知度與產業歷史。我們是美國首屈一指的鹹味零食製造商，生產廣泛的鹹味零食產品，包括馬鈴薯片、玉米片、椒鹽卷餅、奶酪零食、豬皮、酒吧/派對混合零食及其他零食。我們的經典品牌組合包含 Utz®、On The Border®、Zapp's®、Boulder Canyon®、Golden Flake®、Hawaiian® Brand 及 Miguelito's® 等，並在美國擁有強大的家庭市佔率，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們的產品可於約 50% 的美國家庭中找到。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們在美國運營八個主要的製造廠，擁有廣泛的生產能力。我們的產品透過直接運送、經銷商及約 2,500 個直接門市配送（DSD）路線，全國性地分銷至超市、量販店、俱樂部、便利商店、藥妝店及其他零售商。我們歷來透過內生擴張及收購來擴大地理範圍與產品組合。根據 2025 年零售銷售數據，我們在阿拉巴馬州、康乃狄克州、特拉華州、路易斯安那州、緬因州、馬裏蘭州、麻薩諸塞州、密西西比州、新罕布夏州、新澤西州、紐約州、北卡羅來納州、俄亥俄州、賓夕法尼亞州、羅德島州、南卡羅來納州、佛蒙特州、維吉尼亞州、華盛頓州及西維吉尼亞州（我們的「核心地理區域」）的 collectively 核心地理區域中，為第二大品牌鹹味零食製造商（我們的「核心地理區域」，以及美國其他所有州為我們的「擴張地理區域」），我們近年已取得強大的區域品牌與分銷能力。

我們的業務受益於多種機會，可帶來有吸引力的長期獲利成長。我們的價值創造策略聚焦於提升生產力以提高毛利率，重新投資於行銷與創新以加速營收成長，並持續進行戰略收購。我們相信我們在鹹味零食產業中擁有長期成長的優勢，因為我們（a）在過去幾年獲得了大量新客戶，（b）在擴張地理區域與未充分滲透的通路有著顯著的成長機會，（c）持續執行生產力措施，我們相信這些措施將有助於推動進一步的行銷與創新，以加速相較於我們競爭對手的銷售成長，（d）持續進行基礎設施改善，以使我們能持續擴張至更高的層次，（e）持續進行戰略收購，這些收購帶來強大的協同效益，並提升我們的競爭地位。我們相信這些成長途徑各自代表著擴大我們淨銷售額的重大機會。此外，我們進一步預期透過供應鏈生產力、營收管理、較高毛利率的產品組合，以及透過利用我們可擴展的現有平台所帶來的增量銷售，長期來看提高我們的毛利率。
本公司已著重於提升製造能力與簡化分銷。在財務年度 2023 年及 2024 年，本公司買斷並終止了多個曾為本公司提供服務的經銷商契約。這些交易分別被計為資產購入及契約終止，並分別導致財務年度終結於 2023 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 29 日的費用為 1.5 百萬美元及 2.1 百萬美元。

2024 年 2 月 5 日，本公司將部分資產與品牌出售給 Our Home™ 的 affiliates，Our Home™ 是 Better-for-You 品牌的營運公司（Our Home）。根據協議，Our Home 的 affiliates 購買 Good Health 及 R.W. Garcia 品牌，以及位於北卡羅來納州林肯頓與賓夕法尼亞州利蒂茨的製造廠及相關資產，並承擔本公司在內華達州拉斯維加斯的廠房租賃及製造業務（Good Health 和 R.W. Garcia 品牌出售），交易金額為 167.5 百萬美元，扣除常見調整後。詳見第 2 註：我們的審計合併財務報表中的資產處置。2024 年 4 月 22 日，本公司也將其位於賓夕法尼亞州柏林與馬薩諸塞州菲奇堡的製造廠及相關資產，包括部分存貨（製造廠出售）出售給 Our Home。

本公司與 Our Home 在 Good Health 和 R.W. Garcia 品牌出售及製造廠出售時，均簽訂過過渡服務協議，這些協議在 2025 年上半年到期。在財務年度 2025 的大部分時間，雙方透過相互製造協議運作。雖然 Our Home 仍參與本公司部分產品的製造，但本公司不再為 Good Health 製造產品。某些 Good Health 產品依分佈協議，繼續透過本公司 DSD 網路為 Our Home 分銷與銷售。本公司從 Our Home 獲得約 18.7 百萬美元的預付款，用以支付這些協議下的服務，本公司將此金額透過營運收入在過渡服務及共製造協議的期間內確認。
作為其持續供應鏈轉型的一部分，本公司於 2025 年 7 月宣佈戰略決策，將其製造基地進行整合，關閉位於密歇根州格蘭德拉普的製造廠。此決策是本公司長期戰略路線圖的重要組成部分，預期將產生成本節省，並有助於本公司將更多產量分配至其規模較大且更高效的製造廠，同時提升其剩餘網路的固定成本效益與自動化能力。除了預期的成本節省外，本公司預期優化後的製造基地將支持其持續的地理擴張。
2025 年 9 月，本公司宣佈了一項分階段的計畫，旨在提升位於賓夕法尼亞州漢諾威校區的廠房。該計畫包括升級本公司總部，並轉型為現代員工中心，以及其他升級措施。作為該計畫的一部分，本公司有意出售位於賓夕法尼亞州漢諾威的兩棟大樓。詳見第 5 註：廠房、廠房及設備，淨值。

我們有長期成長策略，著重於各種計畫。我們的投資組合策略聚焦於加速在行銷與創新上的投資，以推動營收成長並在鹹味零食類別中取得市佔率。我們計畫進一步深入我們的擴張地區與未開發通路與客戶，透過進一步擴展我們在擴張地區的自有品牌鹹味零食（如下所定義），同時維持我們在核心地區的市佔率。我們計畫將供應鏈轉型為更具成本效益且靈活的系統。根據我們的長期成長策略，我們意圖強化我們的DSD系統，以進一步提升執行效率並產生更高回報，同時強化其他組織能力並降低成本。此外，我們意圖透過加速現金產生並維持嚴謹的資本配置方式，來改善資產負債表的靈活性，這將降低槓桿率，同時在合適時機追求戰略性的收購與處分。

本公司業務由一個運營部門管理與報告，這是因為本公司銷售的所有產品性質相似，組織結構的功能性對齊，以及經常被首席運營決策者（"CODM"）審閱的報告，用以評估績效與分配資源。然而，我們戰略性地管理我們的品牌組合，將我們唯一的運營部門分為自有品牌鹹味零食與非自有品牌及非鹹味零食。整體而言，自有品牌鹹味零食具有較高的成長與毛利率，較大的價值創新潛力，以及對消費者行銷的較佳反應能力，相較於非自有品牌及非鹹味零食。因此，我們將投資支出與品牌建設活動集中於自有品牌鹹味零食，同時管理非自有品牌及非鹹味零食以產生現金流，以支持自有品牌鹹味零食的投資並資助其他企業優先事項。我們定期評估這些分類中品牌之指定，並根據其與上述標準的對齊情況重新分類品牌。

我們的自有品牌鹹味零食包含我們的Power Four品牌，包括我們的旗艦品牌Utz®、On The Border®、Zapp's®與Boulder Canyon®，以及我們的其他品牌，包括Golden Flake®、Miguelito's®、Hawaiian®、Bachman®、Tim's Cascade®、Dirty Potato Chips®、TGI Fridays®與Vitner's®（我們的"其他品牌"）。

我們的旗艦品牌Utz在2025年的零售銷售額超過870百萬美元，代表約5.7%的複合成長率（"CAGR"）（2021年至2025年），使其成為截至2025年12月28日根據Circana資料，美國零售銷售額前10大的鹹味零食品牌之一。自1920年代以來，Utz品牌以其標誌性的"小Utz女孩"標誌而聞名，目前使用口號"家族手工調味，自1921年起"。我們在Utz品牌下銷售多種鹹味零食，包括薯片、鯛魚絲、奶酪零食、派對混合零食以及季節性熱門商品。
我們的On The Border品牌（"OTB"）為全國知名的玉米片、莎莎醬與奶酪品牌。OTB根據截至2025年12月28日財務年度的年度銷售額，為美國第二大無添加味玉米片品牌。OTB支持我們的全國地理版圖，特別是在我們的擴張地區，並增強我們在大賣場與俱樂部零售通路的現有地位。

Garcia 品牌，以及位於北卡羅來納州林克爾頓與賓夕法尼亞州利蒂茨的製造廠與部分相關資產，並承擔本公司在內華達州拉斯維加斯的廠房租賃與製造作業（"Good Health 與 R.W. Garcia 儲備"），交易金額為 167.5 百萬美元，並受制於慣例調整。詳見附註 2。出售至我們的審計合併財務報表。於 2024 年 4 月 22 日，本公司亦將其位於賓夕法尼亞州柏林與馬薩諸塞州菲奇堡的製造廠與部分相關資產，包括部分存貨出售給 Our Home（"製造廠出售"）。

本公司與 Our Home 針對 Good Health 與 R.W. Garcia 儲備與製造廠出售，均簽訂過過渡服務協議，這些協議於 2025 年上半年到期。在 2025 年財務年度的大部分時間，雙方則根據相互製造協議運作。雖然 Our Home 仍參與本公司部分產品的製造，但本公司不再為 Good Health 製造產品。部分 Good Health 產品依分佈協議，繼續透過本公司 DSD 網路為 Our Home 分銷與銷售。本公司從 Our Home 獲得約 18.7 百萬美元的預付款，用以支應這些協議下的服務，本公司已將此金額透過營運收入確認，並於過渡服務與共製造協議的期間內確認。

作為其持續供應鏈轉型的一部分，本公司於 2025 年 7 月宣佈，決定將其製造設施與位於密歇根州格蘭德拉普的製造廠關閉，以實現製造設施的整合。此決定是本公司長期戰略路線圖的重要組成部分，預期將產生成本節省，並使本公司能將更多產量分配至其規模較大且更高效的設施，同時提升其剩餘網路的固定成本槓桿與自動化能力。除了預期的成本節省，本公司預期優化後的設施將支持其持續的地理擴張。於 2025 年 12 月，本公司出售其位於密歇根州格蘭德拉普的製造廠；然而，本公司隨後與買方簽訂租賃協議，並目前持續在該廠運作。詳見附註 5。固定資產、廠房與設備，淨值。
於 2025 年 9 月，本公司宣佈一項分階段的計畫，旨在提升其位於賓夕法尼亞州漢諾威校區的設施。此計畫包括升級本公司總部，並轉型為現代員工中心，以及其他升級措施。作為此計畫的一部分，本公司有意出售位於漢諾威、賓夕法尼亞州的三棟建築物。詳見附註 5。固定資產、廠房與設備，淨值。
作為加州擴張策略的一部分，於 2025 年 10 月，本公司取得 Insignia International 的 DSD 分銷資產。此交易包括加州與中西部的 DSD 路線，以及部分相關資產。此收購加速了 Utz 在加州的擴張，加州是關鍵成長地區，代表美國鹹味零食最大的市場，根據 Circana 資料，零售銷售額為 4.2 十億美元。
在截至 2024 年 12 月 29 日的財務年度內，本公司買斷並終止多個第三方分銷商的合約，這些分銷商先前曾為本公司提供服務。這些交易被視為合約終止與資產購入，導致截至 2024 年 12 月 29 日的財務年度產生 2.1 百萬美元的費用，並包含於合併損益與綜合損益（虧損）表中。

投資於新產品創新支持三個重點領域，這些領域根植於消費者需求，並與我們的產品組合與品牌策略相關：擴展正面選擇、提供令人渴望的風味，以及捕捉時機。在擴展正面選擇方面，近期的重點為 Boulder Canyon，這是一個提供解決方案的品牌，針對尋求美味 BFY 零食的消費者，透過 BFY 油脂如牛油果油與橄欖油。創新促成了 Boulder Canyon® 的成長，透過推出新口味，抓住熱門的辣味趨勢，並進入乳酪零食子類別。根據 Circana 資料，Boulder Canyon® 在截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日的財務年度中，與去年同期相比成長 180.5%。在自然通路中，Boulder Canyon 的成長為 36.9%，根據 Spins 資料。在提供令人渴望的風味方面，我們近期透過創新，針對消費者對風味探索的渴望，透過我們的經典椒鹽餅與新馬鈴薯片風味產品，於 Utz 與 Zapp's 品牌中推出。在捕捉時機方面，我們近期推出一系列多包裝產品，涵蓋我們的 Power Four 品牌，包括我們的旗艦 Utz® 品牌、On The Border®、Zapp's® 與 Boulder Canyon®，以及我們的 Targeted 品牌，包括 Golden Flake®、Miguelito's®、Hawaiian®、Bachman®、Tim's Cascade®、Dirty Potato Chips® 與 TGI Fridays®。在 2025 年第三季，我們宣佈承諾於 2027 年底前從我們的產品組閤中移除食品、藥物與化妝品顏色。雖然我們目前不預期在努力達成此承諾時對我們的投入成本產生重大影響，但若我們未能成功持續滿足消費者偏好，則我們的銷售額、市佔率或營運結果可能受到不利影響。

我們定期監測全球供應與原物料成本，以確保能以成本效益的方式取得生產所需的原料、包裝與燃料。許多外部因素，如天氣，可能因氣候變遷而以未預期的方式受到影響，原物料市場狀況、通貨膨脹條件以及政府、農業或其他計畫（包括關稅或其他貿易政策）的影響，可能影響我們產品所使用的原料與農產品的成本與可得性。由於我們幾乎所有的投入成本均來自國內，且所有製造廠均位於美國，我們繼續預期近期關稅波動對我們 2026 年的業務將產生輕微且可管理的影響。我們主要透過買斷（buying-forward）來應對原物料成本，這項做法可於三至十八個月內鎖定關鍵材料的價格。其他方法包括套期保值、透過長期成本通貨膨脹調整的淨價格調整，以及製造與營運成本控制。我們的套期保值技術，如遠期合約，可限制我們主要原物料成本波動的影響；然而，我們可能無法完全對抗原物料成本變動，特別是在無法套期保值的情況下，且我們的套期保值策略可能無法保護我們免於特定原物料成本的上升。原物料成本上升可能對我們的淨收入產生不利影響。雖然我們經歷了一些原料成本的下降，但我們持續面臨燃料與運輸費用上升的問題，以及勞動成本上升，這些均對利潤率產生負面影響。運輸成本持續上升，可能繼續上升並對淨收入產生不利影響。本公司透過提高製造與分銷效率，以及對客戶提高價格，來抵消成本上升，但尚不清楚在這些較高價格下，歷史客戶銷售水平是否能維持（詳見 "關鍵發展與趨勢 - 長期人口統計、消費者趨勢與需求" 以及 "關鍵發展與趨勢 - 競爭"）。由於競爭市場條件、計畫中的貿易或促銷激勵措施或其他因素，我們的價格調整措施可能也會落後於供應與原物料成本的變動。
{'translated_text': '雖然我們主要原物料的價格會有波動，我們認為這些原物料的供應將持續充足，且通常會從多個來源取得。市場因素，包括供給與需求，可能會導致這些原物料的採購成本提高。'}

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們經營於高度競爭且持續集中化的零食食品產業。若我們無法有效競爭，可能會降低我們向客戶或消費者銷售產品的能力。
對我們產品的需求可能因消費者偏好或口味的變化，或我們無法有效創新或行銷產品而受到不利影響，這可能會降低我們的營業收入。
消費者對我們品牌的忠誠度可能因我們無法控制的因素而改變，這可能會對我們的業務及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
若我們的產品受到污染或標籤錯誤，我們可能需要召回這些產品，並可能面臨產品責任索償及相關損失，以及對我們聲譽的損害。
零售分銷安排的變化可能導致零售架位的喪失，並幹擾食品產品的銷售，造成我們的銷售額下降。
電子商務零售商及銷售通路的演進可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生不利影響。
我們製造運作、供應鏈或分銷通路的中斷，可能會影響我們生產或交付成品的能力，並對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險與不確定性。您應仔細考慮下列風險，以及本年度報告表10-K所包含的其他資訊。我們營運於一個不斷變化的環境中，涉及許多已知與未知的風險與不確定性，這些可能對我們的營運造成重大不利影響。任何下列風險都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果或前景造成重大且不利的影響。然而，下列所選取的風險並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，但這些也可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果或前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司證券的交易價格可能會下跌，您可能會損失全部或部分投資於我們的資金。
我們大多數產品的銷售受到顯著競爭的影響，這是因為產品品質與風味、消費者對品牌的認知度、零售客戶場地的貨架空間取得、價格、廣告與促銷、時尚零食的創新、提供的零食種類、營養成分、產品包裝與包裝設計等因素所致。我們在零食食品市場上與許多國際性、區域性與地方性公司競爭，包括在BFY產品子類別中，主要根據產品風味與品質進行競爭，但也包括品牌認知度與忠誠度、價格、行銷、廣告以及滿足特定消費者飲食需求的能力。

由於零食食品產業的競爭態勢，我們所發起的產品價格上漲或未能有效廣告與促銷產品，若未被我們的客戶、IOs、第三方經銷商或消費者妥善實施或接受，可能會對我們的財務結果造成負面影響。維持或改善我們品牌市場地位或推出新產品至市場，可能需要大量廣告與促銷支出。產業參與者可能正在進行新的廣告趨勢或渠道，而我們尚未參與。歷來，我們已為客戶、IOs、第三方經銷商與消費者提供多種銷售與促銷激勵措施，例如價格折扣、消費者紅利券、採購量回扣、合作行銷計畫、產品置放費用與店內展示，常與季節性社會活動、節日與體育賽事結合。近年來，促銷環境已更加激烈，包括但不限於強力的促銷發動，我們已並可能在未來受到限制，無法在及時或完全的基礎上提高價格或調整產品尺寸，以抵消增加的投入成本，例如原材料、包裝、能源、運輸、勞動與間接費用或其他支出，例如廣告與促銷費用，這會導致整體銷售量、收入與營運獲利減少。此外，若消費者優先考慮價格而非其他因素，並購買較低成本的替代品，例如自有品牌、通用或商店品牌產品，則廣告與促銷支出可能無效。

我們的競爭能力也可能取決於零售客戶場地是否有適當的零食類別貨架，以及我們的產品是否放置在適當的零食貨架上，例如BFY零食食品貨架或傳統零食食品貨架。市場上對BFY產品及其他專門產品的關注度不斷增加，未來期間這些競爭壓力可能進一步增加。此外，BFY產品領域的公司若提供創新或時尚的零食食品，往往會獲得私人股權、風險投資或其他投資者的投資，這些投資者可能更願意接受較低的產品毛利或持續虧損，以獲得市場份額。若這些新興公司能透過更創新或時尚的零食食品吸引忠實消費者，或以較低價格提供零食食品，我們的市場份額與營運結果可能受到重大且不利的影響。
若我們的廣告或促銷努力未能提高品牌知名度或增加產品銷售，我們的費用可能增加而收入未相應增加，導致營運獲利減少。此外，若某些投入材料的市場價格大幅下降，我們可能因合同關係而需支付客戶差價，或因客戶壓力而降低產品價格，這可能會降低我們的收入與營運獲利。

零食食品產業持續進行合併，零售端的零食食品通路也由其他市場參與者進行合併。雖然我們受益於在零食食品產業內執行自己的收購策略，以及在零食分銷通路的相關策略，但產業持續合併，或零售客戶或潛在零售客戶與長期採購契約或促銷安排，可能會使我們無法有效競爭，特別是當產業中擁有較多資源的公司，或零售客戶或潛在零售客戶與長期採購契約或促銷安排。其他參與者的重大合併會增加我們可能失去一個或多個主要客戶、失去現有產品授權或零售客戶場地的貨架空間，或失去市場份額的可能性。例如，我們的競爭對手爭取相同的貨架空間，並可能提供零售客戶我們無法匹配的激勵措施，特別是因合併所致。即使我們獲得貨架空間或優先的貨架位置，我們的新產品與現有產品可能未能達到零售客戶設定的銷售預期，這可能會導致這些零售商將我們的產品從貨架上移除，或放置在較不利的位置。此外，我們競爭的產品類別中私人品牌產品的數量與品質增加，已減少可用貨架空間，並可能持續影響我們品牌產品的擺放位置，這可能會對我們的銷售造成不利影響。為取得並維持我們產品的貨架空間，我們可能需要增加行銷與廣告支出，以創造消費者認知、保護並擴大現有市場份額或推廣新產品，這可能會影響我們的營運結果。我們也持續評估產品線，以判斷是否需要終止某些產品。終止產品線可能提高我們的獲利，但可能減少銷售，並影響品牌與消費者忠誠度，而某些產品銷售減少可能導致其他產品銷售也減少。
